title: Acute Symptoms of Tear Gas Exposure and Adverse Reproductive Health Outcomes in Males
content: Exposure to tear gas, a chemical agent used primarily to disperse crowds, results in acute adverse effects on health which are well-documented but may have longer-term impacts on health. This study investigated the association between tear gas exposure during protests in 2020 and male reproductive health outcomes. Data were collected through an anonymous online questionnaire in 2020–2021 from adults exposed to tear gas. Exposure was assessed using reported acute symptoms affecting the eyes, lungs, skin, and heart. A symptom-based exposure score ranging from 0–14 was categorized as low, medium, or high. Male participants reported whether they experienced erectile dysfunction, ejaculatory dysfunction, or difficulty conceiving following exposure. Logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Among 92 male respondents, approximately 46% reported at least one reproductive issue, including 28 with erectile dysfunction and 26 with ejaculatory dysfunction. High tear gas exposure was significantly associated with erectile dysfunction compared with low exposure (adjusted OR=6.57; 95% CI: 1.28–40.08). No significant association was observed for ejaculatory dysfunction (adjusted OR=1.96; 95% CI: 0.35–11.36). These findings suggest potential reproductive health effects of tear gas exposure and may help to guide public policy and education.
